podcast.title: Personal Experiences Reflected in "Small Town Boy"
podcast.body: As the singer for Bronski Beat, Jimmy Somerville's personal experiences, including bullying, estrangement from family, and rejection, directly informed and were portrayed in the powerful song and video for "Small Town Boy." "Jimmy Somerville, who by the way experienced the same sort of things that we see in the video, the bullying, the estrangement from family, and the rejection."

xref.title: Early Life and Music Career
xref.body: Richard Coles began his musical journey as a choir boy and later moved into theater. He became the keyboardist for the "groundbreaking gay positive band" Bronski Beat in the early 80s, and then followed singer Jimmy Somerville to form The Communards, where he also played keyboards. "Growing up, he was a choir boy before moving on to theater."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Groundbreaking Gay Positive Band
xref.body: Bronski Beat was recognized as a groundbreaking "gay positive band" in the early 1980s, featuring Richard Coles on keyboards and Jimmy Somerville as the singer. "That eventually led to a job playing keyboards for the groundbreaking gay positive band Bronsky beat in the early 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jimmy Somerville's Personal Connection to "Small Town Boy"
xref.body: The video for "Small Town Boy" featured singer Jimmy Somerville, who personally experienced the same kinds of bullying, estrangement from family, and rejection depicted in the song and its visual narrative. This personal connection added authenticity and emotional weight to the song's message. "You couldn't help but feel terrible for the character played by singer Jimmy Somerville, who by the way experienced the same sort of things that we see in the video, the bullying, the estrangement from family, and the rejection."
